Ashara gives a short nod and returns to her plate.

The conversation drifts with the meal. Thessaly wins an argument with Aldric over whether a spilled drink counts as an accident if someone has been warned three times not to gesticulate near it. Caelindra continues her quiet war against the glazed roots. Ysolde asks the server for the remaining rare slices of roast, and receives them without comment.

When the last plates are cleared, Rashid rises and smooths his cuffs.

“I owe people cards,” he says to Ashara.

“You do.”

He heads for the common room. Dena’s voice carries from beyond the arch: “There he is. Deal him in before he invents another obligation.”

Ashara stands more slowly, collecting the practice jacket she left over the back of her chair. “I’ll use the empty octagon.”

Seraphel looks toward the firelit room.

“The cards appear loud.  
I may prefer to listen  
from somewhere else.”

Then Ashara looks at you.

“Are you coming to watch, or staying here?”
